messages:
maria: Heads-up - spotted a perf regression on the Triton kernel path for long sequences with high KV-cache hit rates. p95 went from ~72ms -> ~81ms on H100 for seq=8192, batch=1, kv_hit~0.9. Throughput steady but tail latency degrading. :thinking:
kevin: Can you dump the profiler output? timeline + kernel names would help. Any change in autotuner picks recently?
maria: Paste of the hot slice from nvprof/Triton profiling:```
[2026-03-14 11:02] kernel:triton_gemm_sliced_sm89  time: 46.2ms
[2026-03-14 11:02] kernel:cutlass_wmma_sm80  time: 39.1ms
[2026-03-14 11:02] kernel:triton_prefix_kv_copy  time: 5.0ms
KV-prefetch/concat overhead: ~6ms per request (small copies)
Total p95 ~81ms
```
liz: Interesting that Triton GEMM is slower here than the CUTLASS path on the same hw. Could be launch/config mismatch for very long seqs + tiny per-step work due to frequent KV pulls.
josh: Autotuner currently uses (arch, batch_size, seq_len, dtype) as feature vector. We never included kv_hit_rate nor avg_prefix_len. If KV hits add lots of tiny memcpy/launches, the autotuner will still pick the 'efficient' kernel for dense compute but miss the microkernel overhead.
maria: I also checked A100 vs H100: A100 favored cutlass for these cases historically; H100 autotuner picked triton_gemm_sliced_sm89 after the latest kernel update. Could be that Triton's optimized path assumes contiguous large matmuls, but with high KV hits we fragment work.
natalie: Two quick hypotheses: 1) KV cache reads create lots of small device-to-device copies that break streaming; 2) Triton kernel is using an algorithm tuned for long contiguous batches, but KV access pattern makes effective tile sizes tiny.
perf-bot: Uploaded full flamegraph + kernel timeline: https://internal.perf/redwood/flame/1765493021 (contains sample timeline and per-kernel latencies) :eyes:
kevin: Short-term mitigation: we can add a routing override to fall back to CUTLASS when seq_len>=4096 && kv_hit_rate>=0.7 on H100. That should reduce tail while we root-cause. Would prefer a heuristic in the autotuner though.
liz: Agree. Also try coalescing KV pulls into larger batched copies (kv_chunk_size) so kernels see bigger contiguous buffers. That often reduces launch overhead.
josh: Proposal for autotuner change: expand feature vector to include: [arch, sm_version, batch_size, seq_len, kv_hit_rate_bucket, avg_prefix_len_bucket, dtype, hw_mem_bandwidth_est]. Then add latency penalty term for "small contiguous compute slices" measured from runtime profiling.
maria: Example routing policy tweak I tested locally:```json
{"routing_override": [{"arch":"sm89","min_seq":4096,"min_kv_hit":0.7,"preferred_kernel":"cutlass_wmma_sm80","reason":"mitigate triton tail on high-kv workloads"}]}
```
Result: p95 dropped to ~74ms on the same workload (one-off test), p50 unchanged.
natalie: Nice. Add a canary rollout in the console with 5% traffic to dedicated and watch regressions. Also log the chosen kernel + kv_hit_rate so autotuner can learn.
deploy-bot: Canary pinned: routing_override applied to staging cluster with id stg-3. Monitoring for 1h and alert on any p99 > 120ms.
kevin: Follow-ups: 1) Add kv_hit_rate sampling into request metadata (already cheap) 2) Emit micro metrics: small_copy_count, avg_copy_size, kernel_launch_count per request 3) Feed to autotuner offline training.
maria: Will open a PR with the routing override + sampling change. I'll attach benchmark scripts. Thanks for rapid feedback. :thumbsup:
